Speechless. This is the future of AI agents

Google Antigravity swarms spun up 7 Gemini Neon agents to all tackle a single problem

They're working on my app testing different ways to architect it

For me, I'm having my swarm test many different system prompts for an agent I'm building, then measuring results

Hit enter, then toggle the overview panel in the top right and go to plugins > swarms so you can watch your swarm work

In the near future, EVERYONE will have their own agent swarms working for them

hits.name: dharmesh
hits.text:
Notes From the HubSpot Refounding, Day 14 (Wed, Nov 25):

I've been spending a lot of time today *thinking* about strategy and market opportunity. 

Here's what's rattling around in my brain:

Agentic Coding has been a massive use case for AI and has produced a ton of economic value for the companies that built those products. I'm not surprised, because the output of agentic coding is...code. And that code (software) can be used to do economically valuable things -- including *selling* that software and getting revenue.

The value is amplified because historically it has been hard and expensive to create software. Historically, humans have had to write code manually. Like cave people! Not any more, we have the tools so humans can be more productive and produce better software faster.

Now, time for a logical leap...

Another thing that is economically valuable and hard to create is...growth. And by growth, I mean in the business sense. Making sales/revenue/customers go up. Historically, humans have had to create things like marketing campaigns, inbound lead workflows and other "artifacts" that then helped drive revenue growth. 

In the world of agentic coding, you need a great purpose-built harness + a great LLM + context (the code  + special skills + design guides) and a system of record (code repo) to produce the outcome needed.

In the world of agentic growth, you need a great purpose-built harness + a great LLM + context (system of record + a second brain for the organization) in order to produce the outcome needed.

And this is what we're focused on at HubSpot with the refounding.

We're building the world's best purpose-built GTM harness which uses a mix of great LLMs + an AI-native context store (CRM database + second brain). 

The HubSpot mission is to help millions grow better.

The way we do that is to help humans responsible for delivering growth to leverage AI for the painful, manual stuff. And just like agentic coding hasn't killed the software builder, agentic growth doesn't kill the need for the high-agency marketing, sales person and revenue leaders. 

Just thinking out loud. What do you think?

#HubSpotRefounding
hits.hook: Notes From the HubSpot Refounding, Day 14 (Wed, Nov 25):  I've been spending a lot of time today *thinking* about strate
hits.draft_en:
Dharmesh Shah, Day 14 of the HubSpot 'refounding': agentic coding produced so much value because its output, code, is directly sellable (20k views).

Look for other jobs where the agent's output is itself the product. That's where the next big agent use cases probably are.
hits.video_tip: 8s: notebook page titled 'output = product?', ticking through job examples.

outsiders.name: Andrej Karpathy
outsiders.text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

outsiders.name: Artificial Analysis
outsiders.text:
Launching our leaderboard for FrontierPhysics, including 54 physics research tasks written by physicists. Claude Fable 5.2 leads at 32%, 6 points ahead of GPT-6.2 Astra

FrontierPhysics is a physics research benchmark from @benchflow_ai, and we run 54 of the 56 tasks (excluding two GPU tasks). Each task is written by physicists and requires the agent to review the literature, run simulations and analyses, and submit its results with a manuscript. Tasks span 9 physics domains, from condensed matter to astrophysics, and are private to avoid contamination.

A run passes only if its results pass the task's numeric checks and LLM agent reviewers find no flaw that would prevent publication. A failed run scores 0, and a passing run scores the share of rubric points the reviewers award.

Key takeaways:

➤ Claude Fable 5.2 (max) leads by 6 points, and the next five models score between 22% and 26%: GPT-6.2 Astra (max) 26%, Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) 25%, Claude Opus 5.5 (max) 24%, Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) 23% and GPT-6.2 Sol (max) 22%

➤ Nearly half of Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh)'s runs that pass the numeric checks fail review: Neon passes numeric checks 54% of the time, the most of any model, but only passes review 28% of the time. The rest have a flaw that would prevent publication, such as an invalid simulation setup, a missing derivation or a written conclusion the results don't support

➤ GPT-6.2 Sol (max) and GPT-6.2 Astra (max) sit on the Pareto frontier for score vs. cost: they score 22% at $1.70 per task and 26% at $5.97. Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) and Claude Opus 5.5 (max) score within 3 points of GPT-6.2 Astra (max) at $13.69 and $21.93

Thank you to @xdotli, @bingran_bry and the team at @benchflow_ai for building FrontierPhysics and working with us to bring it to Artificial Analysis.
outsiders.hook: Launching our leaderboard for FrontierPhysics, including 54 physics research tasks written by physicists. Claude Fable 5

outsiders.name: Artificial Analysis
outsiders.text:
Announcing AA-Robotics-Sim v0.1: frontier language models driving our Unitree G1 humanoid

AA-Robotics v0.1 was our first step, with models controlling a robot arm. AA-Robotics-Sim v0.1 is our research preview of the next one: LLMs in native harnesses directly controlling a simulated Unitree G1 humanoid, with a simple objective for each task. We plan to expand from here.

AA-Robotics-Sim details:

➤ 10 tasks in four groups of skills: embodied reasoning, pick and place, assembly, tool use, and mobility

➤ For each task, a model first plays five practice episodes to learn the environment and take notes. It’s then evaluated on ten new scenes

➤ Every evaluation scene changes the room, the lighting, the layout, the props, and the details of the task

➤ Each episode is scored 0 to 100 from the simulator's measurements, with partial credit

Key results:

➤ GPT-6.2 Astra leads with 71.0, 13.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 (57.5) and GPT-6.2 Sol (53.7), followed by Claude Opus 5.5 (48.2), Gemini 4 Neon (46.2), GPT-6 Astra (46.1), Gemini 4 Argon (45.5), GPT-6.1 Sol (33.1) and Claude Fable 5.1 (29.1)

➤ Some skills are mature; others are missing from every model: every model walked to the goal without moving a package in every navigation episode, but only five dishes ended up in the dishwasher rack in 90 episodes

➤ An evaluation episode takes 17 to 39 minutes and costs $0.84 to $9.01, yet the robot moves for under a minute of it

outsiders.name: Guillermo Rauch
outsiders.text:
As AI gets smarter, implementation details blur away: permissions, code diffs, commands, tool calls…

The harness itself blurs away. It's a high-performance vehicle for code and command execution, and a durable storage engine.

All of fx still fits in 6mb: subagents, MCP, skills, sessions, durability, ACP, TUI, network transport…

Pieter Levels: a lot of founders now need the hard conversation that their business may have no reason to exist anymore (132k views, 810 bookmarks). swyx: SaaS founders are visibly 'refounding' decade-old companies.

Do the 10-minute version today: list what customers could rebuild with an agent, then what they'd still pay you for.

virals.video_tip: 9s: two columns, 'agent can rebuild' vs 'they still pay for', the second one short but bold.

virals.draft_en:
Alex Finn ran 7 Gemini Neon agents on one problem in Google Antigravity '/swarm', then let an orchestrator pick the winner (103k views, 1.3k bookmarks).

Best use: questions with many valid answers. System prompts, architectures, landing copy. Parallel tries plus one clear metric beats one long chat.

virals.video_tip: 8s: 7 tiles running, scores appear, one tile glows as winner.

virals.angle: Neon is the model of the week
virals.draft_en:
Gemini Neon's usage is spiking: Logan Kilpatrick posted 📈📈📈 (460k views), Perplexity says it doubled day over day past 100B tokens, and the open-source Gemini API CLI plugs it into any coding agent (282k views, 1.6k bookmarks).

Don't switch on hype. Run your 3 most common prompts on it and compare cost and output.

virals.draft_en:
OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage was mistakenly discounted at launch. Now fixed: you'll hit plan limits about 40% faster than last week (Tibo, 4.6M views). Banked resets are back online.

If your workflow leaned on those limits, re-route long or batch jobs to a cheaper model now, before you hit the wall mid-task.
virals.video_tip: 7s: a usage bar filling faster, then splitting jobs onto a second model.

virals.draft_en:
Pieter Levels thinks Zapier is a perfect buy for Anthropic or OpenAI: 10,000+ integrations straight into their agents (90k views). Karpathy had Claude pull 31 public data sources into one working map over 7 hours.

Agents are only as useful as what they can reach. If you build a product, a clean API or MCP endpoint is now a distribution channel.

virals_narrative: Window Wed Nov 25 ~11:15 CT through Thu Nov 26 ~11:15 CT (Thanksgiving; outsiders from Tue Nov 24 ~11:15 CT, posts shown Nov 25 left out). 20 watchlist originals cleared 5k views from 8 accounts. Logan Kilpatrick led with Gemini Neon: 'Neon usage is 📈📈📈' (460k) and the open-source Gemini API CLI for any coding agent (282k, 1.6k bookmarks), backed by Alex Finn's 7-agent Antigravity swarm (103k, 1.3k bookmarks) and Perplexity reporting 100B+ Neon tokens a day. Pieter Levels drove the other big thread: many businesses may have no reason to exist anymore (132k, 810 bookmarks), echoed by swyx and Dharmesh's HubSpot refounding notes, plus Zapier as an AI-lab acquisition (90k) and a blocklist update (500+ spammers suspended, ~0.1% false positives). Outside the watchlist: OpenAI fixed a GPT-6.2 discount bug so limits hit ~40% faster (4.56M), Karpathy's Claude-built Civ map from 31 data sources (1.47M, 10.8k bookmarks), Anthropic's Python-to-Rust API migration verified by Claude agents (4.13M), and Perplexity Time Machine.
